question: Should this broad protocol-fidelity hardening land together after targeted provider-native evidence, or be split into independently reviewable shared-recorder and provider-specific patches?
rationale: The implementation appears coherent, but only maintainers can accept the upgrade boundary and review blast radius across several provider emulators and shared delivery infrastructure.

options.title: Prove contracts, then merge
options.body: Keep the unified PR and merge after targeted native-client or provider-contract evidence covers the highest-risk identity, host-validation, ingress, recorder, and shutdown paths.

options.title: Split by provider boundary
options.body: Separate shared HTTP and recorder work from provider-specific semantic changes so each compatibility boundary can be accepted and reverted independently.

options.title: Pause broad hardening
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define which currently tolerated protocol deviations should change together.

recommendation.title: Prove contracts, then merge
recommendation.body: Keep the unified PR and merge after targeted native-client or provider-contract evidence covers the highest-risk identity, host-validation, ingress, recorder, and shutdown paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed repository member connected across all affected implementation areas in the available history.
